messages:
sre-bot: ALERT: 3xx->5xx error spike on /v1/generate; smart-routing fallback triggered from us-east -> eu-west, then eu-west fallback back to us-east. loop detected, traffic doubled. auto-throttle not engaging. severity=high :rotating_light:

sre-bot: Samples: repeated client retries with exponential backoff header missing; multiple clients retrying at 1s intervals. approx 2x amplification in last 90s.

maria_oncall: paging in. I'm on it. @jonathan_infra @leo_runtime please join — looks like a routing policy mis-eval?

jonathan_infra: on call, looking at routing logs now. seeing 503s from model-variant v2-quant at us-east-1 pool, failover policy prefers nearest region then cheapest model. fallback path mis-mapped v2-quant -> v1-fp32 which is heavier.

leo_runtime: that mapping is wrong — v1-fp32 is incompatible with sequence-length 4096 workloads, rejecting many requests. The runtime is triggering fallback and then the client retry loop causes double routing.

anya_support: customers reporting increased latency and rate-limited errors, top affected: api-key cust-832 and cust-194. support tier escalating.

maria_oncall: immediate mitigations: 1) disable smart-routing fallback for the affected model (temp) 2) enable circuit breaker for retries 3) notify status page. Agreed?

jonathan_infra: +1. I'm toggling fallback policy via infra API: 
```
curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/v1/policies/route/disable
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
  -d '{"policy_id":"smart-route-fallback-v2","target": "model" }'
```
I'll set to manual failover only.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: disable-policy smart-route-fallback-v2 by jonathan_infra (rollout 100%)

leo_runtime: while that's rolling, we should also throttle incoming retries with a short-term token bucket for API keys showing >5 retries/s. I can push a config to the edge router.

jonathan_infra: rollback of fallback policy completed — smart-routing fallback set to manual for v2 variants. environment: prod.

maria_oncall: applying retry-suppression rule at edge now. rule: honor X-Request-Id and X-Retry-Count; drop if retry-count > 3 within 30s.

leo_runtime: pushed edge rule. snippet: 
```
edge.rate_limit.add_rule({
  "match": {"path": "/v1/*"},
  "action": "suppress_retries",
  "window": 30,
  "max_retries": 3
})
```

anya_support: messaging update for status page: "Investigating elevated errors for some model generation requests. Mitigations in progress."

statusbot: STATUS PAGE UPDATED: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/185999 - Investigating -> Partial outage

maria_oncall: monitoring metrics — error rate trending down but still above baseline for some tenants. latency back to normal for others.

jonathan_infra: found misconfiguration in routing policy rules: a regexp used to match model family returned empty on long model names, so fallback selected the default variant which is v1-fp32. Putting explicit exact-match rule to avoid that.

leo_runtime: pushing fix to runtime match table now; this will stop incorrect fallback selection.

deploy-bot: runtime config change applied by leo_runtime (canary 10%)

maria_oncall: canary looks good; errors in canary reduced to baseline. rolling to 100%.

leo_runtime: 100% rollout complete. routing no longer pointing to v1-fp32 for v2 requests.

jonathan_infra: I've also raised the circuit-breaker threshold to avoid immediate fallback on transient load spikes; will monitor.

maria_oncall: support, prepare a targeted customer message to the top 5 impacted accounts offering credits and an RCA-to-follow. anya_support, can you draft?

anya_support: on it. draft coming in #customer-comms: "We experienced elevated errors and latency due to an internal routing fallback loop combined with aggressive client retries. We mitigated by disabling automatic fallback and applying retry suppression. We're investigating long-term fixes and will follow up."

maria_oncall: good. timeline so far: 
- 1859991200: small spike detected by SLO monitors
- 1859991234: automated fallback triggered due to 503s from v2-quant
- 1859991268: client retries amplify traffic -> region failover begins
- 1859991320: pager fired, on-call notified
- 1859991370: disable fallback policy (manual)
- 1859991402: edge retry suppression enabled
- 1859991485: routing rule fix rolled to 100%
- 1859991600: errors back to baseline

maria_oncall: current status: mitigated, customer impact limited to elevated latency and some 5xx for ~6 minutes for affected tenants. moving to monitoring.

jonathan_infra: root cause hypothesis: routing policy mis-eval (regex->empty) selected an incompatible model variant under failover. Client libraries with aggressive retry semantics (1s jitterless) amplified the fallback loop, causing a thundering herd between regions. Secondary issue: circuit-breaker thresholds were too tight, causing quick bounce to fallback.

leo_runtime: follow-ups: 1) add exact-match routes for model family names 2) expand canary for routing policy changes 3) add automatic detection for region bounce loops 4) improve circuit-breaker heuristics to consider retry headers

anya_support: customer comm sent to affected accounts, offering 10% credit and SLA review.

maria_oncall: closing incident thread soon. leaving open for 1 hour for monitoring. create postmortem ticket pls.

jonathan_infra: created PM ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INC-5421 - includes logs and policy diffs.

maria_oncall: incident resolved -> monitoring. great quick work everyone :tada:.

statusbot: STATUS PAGE UPDATED: Partial outage -> Service degraded (recovery in progress)

maria_oncall: action items assigned in INC-5421: tagging owners: jonathan_infra (routing fixes), leo_runtime (runtime safeguards), platform (client library guidance).

leo_runtime: quick note for postmortem: include a simulation that replays client retry patterns to validate fallback behavior.

maria_oncall: agreed. I'll write the incident summary and timeline in the ticket. moving to post-incident review next week.

sre-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated. duration ~8m. detected amplification factor ~1.9x at peak. automated downstream alerts: auto-closed.
